caption: Here’s a set of stickers I made for a Bunton Bunton GS13 greens mower restoration project.
Made a reproduction vintage dealer sticker for Leiphart Chevrolet for @ghollandram on brushed chrome with a high gloss lamination for extra durability.

Here is the data plate I made for a Bunton GS13 greens mower.   This was made on anodized aluminum then the model and serial number were machine engraved into the surface. #mowerrestoration #vintagemower

1970-1971 Mopar E-body F78-14 Space-Saver spare tire stencil. Found in Dodge Challenger, Plymouth Barracuda, etc.   Someone sells poor reproductions on eBay (the K and 1 are especially bad). I painstakingly traced and vectorized each character to get a perfect reproduction. It took several tries to perfect the spacing. This was cut using a paint mask then airbrushed onto the tire.  #mopar #cuda #b
Here’s a dealer tag I made for @superratchaz for a 1968 C10 Pickup. Printed on chrome mirror.
Here’s a label I made for a KW Hydraulic Lift System (HLS) for @cackbuh . Printed on brush chrome with a clear laminate.
Robin EY15 3.5HP gas engine reproduction labels.  These were printed on a mirror chrome polyester then laminated with a high gloss polycarbonate.

Here’s a set of labels for a Union drill index I made for @the.hobby.garage . These are printed on a gold metallic vinyl to match the original style. I used the auto serialization function to generate each label from an Excel file, but then had to manually modify the smaller fractions sizes.

I made a label for an Athol vise for @balejeune84 . The original was lost and all I had was a low quality photograph of a well worn label. Took some time zooming in and staring to figure out layout. I wasn’t able to find an identical one anywhere online.  This was printed on a 3M metallic gold vinyl and then contour cut to shape.

Made some labels for the automatic roll trackers of a 1917 Style 25 American Fotoplayer (player piano). These were printed on 12 mil synthetic paper, and then cut with a Graphtec. The 3/64” nail holes are too small for my cutter, so I left marks so they could be manually drilled.  I made this for a YouTube piano restoration by Nate Otto. You can check him out on Youtube (Outside the Vacuum).
Here is a Husky-Master lift label reproduction. The lift was blasted and painted and wouldn’t look right with the old label.
General Electric 3/4HP motor label. This label was severely faded, and was nearly impossible to see the details. It was printed and laminated then applied to 0.025” aluminum.

Here is a set of labels I made for a restoration of a vintage John Deere #374 trencher attachment for @popeofjohndeere   This was especially tricky because I only had a distorted photo of each label. Fortunately, I knew the size, so did my best to make an accurate reproduction.  These were printed and brushed aluminum and white, and then a clear polycarbonate lamination was added.

Here’s a reproduction label for a Bridgeport right angle head for @xbrauerx . The original was stripped and powder coated, and looks great with a fresh decal.  This was printed on using 3M 220 High Performance Vast vinyl in gold metallic.

PUSH TO START tag for 1974 Ferrari 246 Dino laser engraved on anodized aluminum for @grandtouringenterprises. This was only used for 1974 US market cars. The original had the upper-right corner clipped, but that will be trimmed to fit during installation.

Just finished up a set of price tags for a vintage Master Lock display board. These were printed on a 12 mil synthetic paper, then cut with a Graphtec flatbed cutter.  The board is getting fully restored. Each piece will be removed and cleaned, and the backboard will be repainted. The final step is putting one of each lock on the board.
Reproduction Baldor 8100W 3/4HP grinder label. The original grinder only had a handwritten label and no rivet holes.  The replacement label was laser engraved on blue anodized aluminum.
Here is a reproduction label I made for a not very vintage Craftsman 8” Bench Grinder 319.190420. This was printed on white adhesive vinyl then laminated with a polycarbonate high gloss material.
A set of Alcoa wheel stickers off a 2015 Ram 3500 for @orangeamcs_  These were printed on a brushed chrome adhesive material

Restoration of a Di-Acro shear No. 3 (12”) with reproduction nameplate. I found this on Facebook marketplace in rough shape for $120. There are several variations of the nameplate and this is one I haven’t seen before. It was laser engraved on lacquered black aluminum then the serial number was diamond scribed using a cnc engraver. I fully disassembled it, stripped it and repainted it with brush o

Made a Delta 23-990 8” bench grinder label. The original label was missing and all he had was the dimension and an angled photo from an auction site. I guess I’m getting old because this doesn’t look so vintage to me!

I found a Beverly throatless shear for a good price on Facebook marketplace, but it was in rough shape. It was fully disassembled and wire wheeled to remove the paint and rust, then a fresh coat of paint was added. Of course I made a replacement label. The original drive screws snapped when the old tag was removed, so new holes were drilled with a #51 bit so that I could use #0 drive screws.  The

Lucas fuel injection plate from a Maserati for @grandtouringenterprises . This is engraved on 0.060” aluminum using a 0.030” engraving bit. It was then color filled with a bake to cure paint for durability and heat resistance.  I had an exact match single stroke font for the small text, then hand drew the Lucas logo. The smaller holes were punched and the larger one was drilled then filed to size.
Here is a Peerless Electric Co motor label. The original one was in very rough shape - all the red faded away. The company logo was manually vectorized to be smooth.
I made a set of reproduction labels for Ramsey winch for @brad_sull . The warning label is made on anodized aluminum while the nameplate was printed and applied to an aluminum sheet.

I made a set of labels for a Skilsaw 107 restoration.  My printer prints one color, then rewinds the material before printing the next. This can cause mis-registration between colors up to 0.030”. Most of the time this isn’t noticeable, but when there’s an overlap between colors, I add a bleed to the top color. You can see an area where both the black and red print on top of each other.

Reproduction Craftsman Vari-Slo Speed Control on 0.020” aluminum to wrap around drill press head. This was made for @alex_m_creations along with a Craftsman badge for a King Seeley press restoration project.

Craftsman badge printed in Intense Red & Cobalt Blue for @alex_m_creations . I use a spot color printer, not an inkjet so each color is a different ribbon. You can see the section of foil that is transferred to the vinyl.

Here is a reproduction label for a Sears Craftsman 113.213170 17” Drill Press made for @brad_sull . Not exactly a vintage piece of equipment, but the original label was severely damaged and made the whole press look bad.

Here is the reproduction tag for a Dayton 1/3HP Bench Grinder. It is laminated with a scuff resistant polycarbonate, then applied to a 0.020” sheet of aluminum with 1/8” holes punched for drive screws.

Reproduction labels for a Di-Acro #4 24” Metal Shear. I purchased this last month in rough shape - it was stored outside and totally seized, and was missing the table. Within a week I had it fully disassembled, repainted, and functioning smoothly. It looks so much better with a nice paint job and a set of fresh labels.  Di-Acro wanted more for a replacement table than I paid for the entire machine

Delta ON/OFF switch tag for a HD shaper. The original was painted over, but some stripper made it visible enough to use as a template. This was printed then applied to a piece of aluminum and then filed to shape.

Schumacher Sure Fire Battery Charger label. This was applied to a piece of aluminum and then filed to exactly match the original, but somehow I lost the photo. This was printed on clear so that the aluminum underneath would show.

Full set of decals for a 1980s Goodall commercial mower. The original tags were damaged and needed to be removed to repaint. The most time-consuming one was the round caution label. It was really tricky to get the dash lines in just the right pattern to match the original. The second trickiest one was one of the smallest. The engine speed required that I draw a turtle and a rabbit.

Valve cover label for a 1950s BMW 507 3.2L for @rbj80 and @eclectic_motor_company . The original has a brownish print. I made reproductions using black anodized aluminum, and made another set by applying printed vinyl to aluminum. That’s a better color match, but may not be as durable.

I made a reproduction label today for a Craftsman 115.6332 1/2 HP Bench Grinder restoration.  After creating a perfect vector layout, I inverted the design to laser it on anodized aluminum. This is because anything black in the design will be lasered away to show the bare aluminum. Then the stamped data was diamond engraved.
Decals for a set of Kennedy toolboxes. I reached out to the manufacturer and they sell every individual part except for this because it’s installed during manufacturing. So I made my own.

Made a set of labels for a Craftsman drill press with Dunlap motor. The black labels were laser engraved on anodized aluminum then the model and serial number where diamond-scribed engraved. The burgundy one was printed and laminated then apply to a sheet of aluminum and filed to shape. The original drive screws were damaged, so have a new set for easy installation.

Rockwell “First in Safety LVC” decal reproduction for @_patmcgowan . LVC is their term for a magnetic starter (Low Voltage Control).  I had a rendering from vintage machinery but it wasn’t very accurate. It was off-center, had an extra black border and had a registration shift between the colors. Plus is was a bitmap with rough edges.   While browsing marketplace I found the label photo. I make my

Reproduction headband for a Rockwell Delta 11-280 Radial Drill Press. This was printed on a gray silver adhesive vinyl then applied to a sheet of aluminum. The small dots at each corner are used to locate the 1/8” holes. The original one was faded and etched.

Reproduction fuse panel label for Iso Grifo Italian grand tourer car restoration. These were only manufactured from 1965-1974 and have a beautiful design.   Printed on brushed silver. Because of the reflective of the substrate, it took several tries to get a good color match. That also made it hard to get a good photo.   It’s interesting that there were only 12 fuses. Four of which are used for th
Circa 1935 Delta 705-222 Triple Duty Grinder label reproduction.
Porter-Cable (Syracuse) Sanders - Grinders - Saws label reproduction laser engraved on black lacquered aluminum. Made for @_patmcgowan for a B3 sander.

Made a set of STARRETT CRYSTAL PINK granite block nameplates for @charlespastor printed on silver vinyl and adhered to a piece of 0.020” thick aluminum sheet. Laminated with a scuff resistant polycarbonate for high durability.
Reproduction Threads Per Inch & Feeds for a vintage LeBlonde lathe. This is laser engraved on black lacquered aluminum, exposing the aluminum below.

Dealer sticker reproduction for SCHEID / Oldsmobile / GMC Trucks / Cadillac. All I had was a low resolution photo of this sticker on a vintage car. Printed on two mill glossy silver poly. It’s hard to get a good photo of a high gloss label. Made for @wgm200smain
Reproduction of a dealership sticker for a 1970 Dodge Challenger. The sticker didn’t survive peeling off so I used the photo to create a perfect recreation.
1942 LeBlond Regal 13” lathe labels for @mikeritchey4 This set of labels was especially challenging. The originals were damaged and I didn’t have a good photograph of them.
Reproduction nameplate labels for a Craftsman drill press 103.23100.

Reproduction label for a 1958 1-Horsepower Craftsman motor from a vintage tablesaw. I’ve never made this exact style before, but was able use components from similar labels to put it together. It was a huge help having a flat scan of it that I could use as a template for sizing and positioning of each element.

Delta 1HP REPULSION-INDUCTION motor label. The original was barely legible, but there was just enough detail for me to see the specifications. This is on an aluminum plate that was hand filed to the exact shape. Like my other tags, it has a scuff resistant polycarbonate lamination.  I make them and ship them flat, but they’re easy to bend into the proper and then can be attached to the motor.

Here is a vintage Delta Catalog No. 800 label I made. It’s printed on a sparkly gold adhesive vinyl with black and red, then I add a scuff resistant lamination. It’s then fed into a vinyl cutter which recognizes alignment marks and cuts precisely around each one.  The original was probably a waterslide decal, and couldn’t be removed without destroying it. I was provided a drawing with measurements

Labels for a Hitachi B600-A bandsaw restoration project for @kiernanwoodworks   If you look closely, you’ll see that the labels have typos and uneven letter spacing. This is intentional so that it matches the originals. (“crearance” “atta” “hight” etc)  These were printed on a silver gray adhesive vinyl, and then laminated with a high gloss film.   They’re kind of ugly, but took a long time to rep

Reproduction labels for a 1945 Delta DP600 17” drill press for @duaneandrew5. The old label was in very rough shape, but by getting measurements and finding similar labels online, I was able to make a perfect reproduction.  These labels are printed on a gold at his vinyl, then laminated for added durability.
Label reproduction for Ace Tap And Die Set for a restoration by @charlespastor. This was printed on clear so you’ll be able to see the wood grain below.

Cutler Hammer Control label. The original was heavily worn and needed to be replaced. This is a very small aluminum label 0.9” square with 5/64” punched holes. This was for a Southbend lathe restoration.

Vintage label for the restoration of a 1985 Goodall G48 Comercial mower. The original tag was missing but I had an image from the manual which helped, plus the dimensions and spacing for the rivets.  This was laser engraved on gloss black lacquered aluminum then manually engraved on a New Hermes pantograph engraver.
Vintage W.W. Grainger emblem for a Blue Star drill press for @jimjaws1961 . All I had was a bad photo of the original damaged tag, and a dimension (1 -3/4” x 1-1/2”)

Paint masks to restore good emblems off a 1970s Mopar. “340 Four Barrel” and “440 Six Pack”.  This had to be very precise to prevent any overspray and took several dozen attempts to tune each character. I don’t usually work with dimensional pieces, and had to pull out the caliper to get the size and spacing of each character perfect.  “Six pack” mask is laser cut card stock (the center of the P &

Replacement labels for the blade guard off a Dewalt radial arm saw. The original label was missing, but I was able to find photos online of what it should look like.  It took a little experimentation to determine the size needed. I made one the original burgundy color on silver, and one as black on silver. These are both on aluminum which was cut and filed to shape, then double sided adhesive was

Western Auto Supply Company label reproduction from a vintage toolbox. The old label could not be peeled off without destroying it, so this was made with a photograph and an overall dimension. (1-15/32”)

I made a set of vintage Estwing hammer labels for @garageshop_minnesota. These are 7/8” x 2-3/4” and printed on clear adhesive vinyl with a scuff resistant lamination. It’s hard to see the details in the final print so I’ve also included an image of the vector version. (I’m behind in posting – these were made back in April). The originals were carefully peeled off the hammer, then scanned to a PDF

Re-created a 1938 Delta 1426 Sander label. The original label was missing, and all we could find were low resolution photos taken at an angle. I saw a similar sander for sale on eBay, and the seller was willing to take a straight on photo and provide some critical measurements which allowed me to create a perfect vector version. Due to the small text size (0.040”) I used a Mimaki solvent based ink
Embossed anodized nameplate for a Craftsman 103.24280 Bandsaw. This is a slight variation of others I made so I had to redo the layout to match. One distinction is a smaller AND.

Made a reproduction TIBON Hard Chrome Ways nameplate for a Bridgeport milling machine. The original was heavily faded, but I had a photo of what it should look like. This was completely hand-drawn as a vector file so I have clean crisp lines.  It’s small, only 1-3/4” wide x 1-3/16” tall with 1/8” rivet holes

Reproduction label for a Delta model Q5002B motor from a 1938 Delta 820 sander.   There are a ton of variations of these labels so I had to redraw a significant portion of it. Everything is drawn as perfect vector lines and curves. Then printed on silver/gray adhesive vinyl before adding scuff resistant overlaminate and mounting onto a sheet of aluminum.
Shopmaster drill press tag reproduction. This was a bit of a challenge, because all I had was a skewed photo and the measurement between the three holes. But it came out great!

Baldor 762R 1/2HP grinder label reproduction. I’ve never seen this style label before with a red border around each spec. Newer labels show “Cycles” instead of “Hz” and list HP in fractions (1/2 vs 0.5). Tried something new - instead of printing on clear and applying over aluminum, I printed on silver/gray and applied to aluminum. Makes for a sharper image with very little difference in color.

Craftsman 100 and 150 drill press headbands. These were really a challenge to make because of the size and complexity of the shape. Each one is almost 24” long. The 100 headband is at the top. It’s made with silver small engine turn applied to aluminum then cut and filed to shape. An almost perfect match. The 150 headband is foil printed with red, black, and white on a gold metallic vinyl, then la

I made a set of data plates for a Military Jeep M725 Ambulance. The originals were in rough shape and one was almost completely faded away. These were all laser engraved using a Trotec Speedy 400 on matte black anodized aluminum, then trimmed and hole punched to be ready for installation. Highly durable finish that won’t fade or wear.

Sioux Tools Valve Grinder reproduction tag. This is one of that larger labels I’ve made at 12” in diameter. Made for @bourdeau_tool_co for a restoration project. All he could provide was a photograph of the original but that was enough to make an accurate reproduction. Printed then a clear gloss lamination was applied. I can’t want to see it installed!
Reproduction switch plate for a vintage Craftsman 12” lathe. These were laser engraved on a flat black anodized aluminum then punched and filed to shape.

Quick label for a 1961 Wilton Cadet vise restoration. Top is original label I peeled off before stripping and painting and below are my reproductions. A coat of spray paint followed by a clear coat and it’s ready to go back into service! I always have a few restorations going on simultaneously.
Made a Will-Burt Versa-Vise label for mrpete222 after seeing him on YouTube do a restoration. The original was in bad shape and couldn’t be reused.
Vintage Baldor label reproduction on an aluminum plate
A batch of Baldor nameplates made for restoration of a grinder.

Baldor PB9 dust collector label reproduction. I fully disassembled the Baldor to replace bad bearings and give it a fresh coat of paint. Usually I try to peel old label off to get a flatbed scan to use as a template but this label broke into tiny pieces. So I had to resort to using a caliper to get measurements then reproduce from that. Printed with black over gold metallic vinyl. Turns out a 1/2H

Reproduction labels for a South Bend 10K metal lathe. These were tedious to recreate in vector format, probably over 6 hours of layout work. Just the South Bend logo at the bottom took over an hour to get perfect. These are 99.9% perfect recreations. One area that is imperfect is the exact spacing of dashed lines in the gearing diagrams.
Craftsman Power Pak switch label reproduced from a photo. To make the yellow more opaque it has a layer of white underneath.
Lubrication Chart reproduction for a South Bend 10K lathe restoration. The original was nearly impossible to read. This was printed on clear, laminated and applied to aluminum.
Reversing switch reproduction for a South Bend 10K lathe restoration. This was printed on clear, laminated and applied to aluminum.
Motor and pulley reproduction labels for a TGY-515 mill with Conde motor (1980s vintage from Taiwan)
Delta Unisaw power switch plate reproduction. Internal slots and holes are time consuming to make. I start by punching some holes through then clean up with small files to perfect the shape.

Cutler Hammer Forward/Reverse switch label reproduction.  Printed on clear, scuff resistant lamination added the applied to a piece of aluminum. The first attempt making the screw holes damaged the label when the bit wandered (I hadn’t noticed that the tip was snapped).

Made a set of Bennett pump tags. The logo took a while to recreate as clean vector paths needed for the highest resolution output. Then the label was applied to a piece of aluminum and hand trimmed then filed to a perfect circle.

Reproduction Delta Rockwell for @bbberglund2783 on aluminum. Hand punched and filed to shape. There is no “before” photo as the original was not available. I found similar models online and did my best to create an accurate layout.
Made a set of labels for @silverthornknife for a Porter Cable 505 sander. This is a great sander that just needed some minor restoration, and a new set of labels made it look like new again.

Embossed labels for Craftsman 103.23900 6” jointer and 103.24511 drill press. Original labels weren’t in great shape so I made reproductions. The trick to keeping the embossing centered is to emboss first, then add label over the aluminum.
Craftsman 1 HP grinder 257.192190 reproduction label printed on brushed chrome (hard to see the brush marks through the lamination)
Craftsman Repulsion Induction Motor (1 HP) reproduction label on aluminum. Never saw this style Craftsman logo before, nor the blue color. So I had to redraw it all from scratch in vector format.

Delta Triple Duty Ball-Bearing Grinder Label for a model W2268B. I made a similar label in May using artwork available on vintagemachinery.org, but that turned out to be only an approximation. This time I had a scan of an original label and was able to make an exact reproduction.
Made a set of labels for a Delta DP220 and a Craftsman motor. Delta label is printed and stamped and Craftsman label is adhesive.
Craftsman 103.24530 drill press model number tag. Embossed on aluminum

R.K. LeBlond lathe patent list label. OCR helped enter the numbers, then I overlayed the text onto the original to see the mistakes to correct. Found an exact match for the font and adjusted the spacing and tabs for perfect alignment
Craftsman 397.19350 3/4HP bench grinder reproduction label

LeBlond Metal Lathe Threads per Inch and Feeds chart reproduction. Printed on clear and applied to aluminum with a scuff resistant lamination added. This took a couple hours of design time to get everything lined up perfectly and figure out what the damaged sections were supposed to be.

FORWARD / OFF / REVERSE label for Rusnok milling machine. Sometimes only a simple label is needed for a restoration. Printed on 3M white with a scuff resistant polycarbonate lamination, then contour cut to size.
Label for a Craftsman 115.19680 1/2 HP motor off a Craftsman 150 Drill press 103.24521. Only photo I had was at an angle so I did my best to size and position the text to match.
Reproduction label for Rockwell 438-02-314-0187 1/2 HP Dual Voltage Single Phase Motor.

1952 M-2268 Delta Triple-Duty Ball-Bearing Grinder reproduction label on aluminum. The original label was missing so I browsed dozens of historic photos of different generations of grinders to find the perfect match.
Reproduction label for Craftsman 1/2 HP grinder 397.19340. Printed on silver gray adhesive backed vinyl and laminated with a scuff resistant polycarbonate material.
Craftsman embossed tag for 203.21770 drill press final product and before trimming

Made a label for @orangeamcs_  for a 1966 Ford tow truck air cleaner restoration. The original photo provided was on a curve so a bit tricky to get sizing right. The V8 logo was the hardest part. Came out great!
HEAVY DUTY Oil Bath Air Cleaner. This is for a 1966 Ford tow truck. Printed on gold vinyl and laminated with velvet finish polycarbonate.
Delta Rockwell motor reproduction label applied to aluminum plate for a 1964 7”grinder restoration project
1950s Craftsman 103.23130 drill press reproduction label embossed on aluminum
Reproduction tag for 7” Delta Rockwell grinder.

Cincinnati Long Arm Buffer/Grinder Badges for @_patmcgowan grinder restoration. These were redrawn as vector paths then printed, laminated, cut, and applied to aluminum sheet that was then shaped and punched.
1970 Plymouth Cuda dealer label reproduction.
Dayton motor label reproduction for @ssninerguy for a South Bend drill press restoration. This was especially tricky to design with the heavy wear.
Reproduction label for Craftsman 103.24550 12” 3 wheeler band saw.

Craftsman 103.24500 drill press model number label. Printed and embossed aluminum to match original. My embossing machine is not exactly the same size, but very close. This is one of the rare situations where I have a physical tag rather than just a photo.
Craftsman POWR-PANL reproduction labels. Printed with Cobalt Blue on Yellow vinyl and laminated with scuff resistant polycarbonate.
Beard and BluePoint Drive-M-All label set for @xbrauerx. These took hours of fine tuning to get an exact match of the logo and tons of text, then printed and laminated.

Reproduction control panel for 1917 Haddorf upright player piano. On gold tone aluminum with scuff resistant overlamination. Trimmed by hand (lots of file work). It’s an exact match to the damaged original. This was made for Nate Otto who has been documenting the restoration in a series of enjoyable YouTube videos. Check them out at https://youtu.be/4ddz7yQvgVs or “nateoutsidethevacuum” channel (I

Rockwell 200v 3 phase motor label reproduction on aluminum. All I had for this was a photo on a curved surface with hard to read data. Made a perfect vector version then printed and applied to a sheet of aluminum that was then filed to exact dimensions.

The main nameplate for a Delta 1160 10” tilt top saw for a restoration by @_patmcgowan - this label was reproduced using spot colors Intense Red and Jet Black then applied to aluminum and trimmed and filed to match the original shape. It was hand drawn in vector format to be an exact match to the original, which was tricky due to the poor condition of the original.

Reproduction labels for Delta 1160 10” tilt top saw. These are for cut depth and angle and show the original labels and my reproduction labels made on aluminum for a restoration by @_patmcgowan - this label was especially tricky to get all the indicator lines at the perfect angle and spacing. Had to utilize Excel to help calculate the angles as my software doesn’t provide a simple method to genera
Vintage Craftsman aluminum nameplate made for @garageshop_minnesota for a restoration project.
Vintage DeWalt brass label for a radial arm saw. These are 4-3/4” x 1-1/4” and laser etched on glossy black lacquered brass for a durable finish.
“Industrial Textile Supply Company” dealer label for Rockwell 127-3549. Printed on clear, laminated and applied to aluminum.

Craftsman 115.6824 1/2 HP motor label reproduction. This is laser etched onto black anodized aluminum to reveal raw aluminum color. The anodized black has a satin finish and is very durable. I can make these in 0.040” and 0.025” thick.
Made a reproduction label for a Craftsman 397.19451 3/4HP grinder. The original label was in rough shape and would not look good with the restoration.

Reproduced a Rockwell 62-610 drill press. The original one was in very bad shape with the center area wiped away. Had make some educated guesses about the shape and proportions of the wiring diagram based on photos of similar machines.
Batch of Baldor grinder labels for a newly restored grinder, along with scans of the original labels that were removed for painting

Seko shaper label. Tried a new technique this time. Made from a piece of 1/8” clear cast acrylic which I laser cut then applied sign vinyl on the back (mirror cut) and double sided adhesive added for mounting onto shaper. Layout was created with a photo found online. It was a simple design so I hand drew the vectors. Last photo shows my tag mounted to the restored shaper.
Craftsman 103.21770 drill press label reproduction made on aluminum plate with embossed numbers. Ready for installation on a machine restoration project.
Craftsman 1/3 HP grinder 397.19391 label. Old label was peeled off during restoration and new label was made to replace it.

Total Shop TS 25-6 Planer label for @the_modsquito to use on a planer restoration. This is printed on clear and applied to aluminum sheet 3-3/4” x 13-3/4”. The layout was easier to work on at a 22° slant, so everything was perpendicular. Then slanted back for printing. Ink used is translucent so that the shimmer of aluminum comes through. All 88 teeth on saw were counted so new one could be drawn
Two replacement embossed Craftsman labels for tools damaged in a fire. 103.22170 table saw and 103.0404 scroll saw. Embossing of 0.024 aluminum plate was done using a vintage Graphotype 6153.

Powermatic labels printed on chrome mirror using UV curable ink for @duckboatsdotnet. The original was embossed but this was printed to simulate the background texture. This is one of the few labels I made with customer supplied artwork.
Made a label for @belair664 for a Craftsman drill press that was missing a label. The numbers are embossed on a piece of aluminum using a vintage Graphotype embossing machine.

Reproduction label for a vintage import planer motor. Found a font that was very close and printed and applied to a sheet of 0.005” aluminum. Adhesive was added to the back so it can be stuck onto the motor housing. @the_modsquito is doing a full restoration of the motor and planer - can’t wait to see it completed!

1953 Baldor grinder label reproduced with a distorted photo and a precise measurement between rivet holes (2-3/4”). Final label is 1-3/4”x3” printed on clear adhesive vinyl, laminated with scuff resistant lamination and applied to a 0.024” sheet of aluminum. Then trimmed, rounded and punched.

Reproduction of vintage Delta Milwaukee motor label applied to an aluminum plate. This was reproduced with a photo and a couple measurements and I had to refer to a photo of a similar motor to see the red wiring diagram which completely wore off the original. Sizing was perfect and it was installed with original drive screws into original holes.

Baldor 1250 2HP buffer reproductionlabel. This is the vintage color to match what the original would have looked like when new in 1985. Printed with Jet Black and Cobalt Blue spot colors on clear then applied to a piece of 0.020” aluminum plate and corners rounded and holes punched. Original drive screws were reused to attach label.
Craftsman 115.7575 grinder label direct printed on aluminum and stamped with original data. This label was from a 1959 model that was in need of restoration.
Timken Bearing label from Craftsman / Atlas metal lathe. This one is small but took hours to fine-tune to match the original font and design.

I just completed this label for a Wilton cutoff bandsaw. This one is large, about 4-1/2” x 10”. This was carefully vectorized - took a while to ensure each character was symmetrical and aligned. Printed with a small choke in the red to ensure overlap between red and black (you can see that overlap if you look closely at the text). Printed on silver adhesive and laminated.

Rockwell motor label for 83-311. The original was very heavily worn and it took a while to figure out how to draw the wiring diagram. I took some educated guesses and it looks great! Once the motor is repainted, this label can be installed over original metal badge, or stuck directly onto the motor.

Saylor-Beall air compressor tank label. Last photo is of the original (on my compressor). This label was especially difficult to design since I had to make compounds (holes) for anything gold and use a spot color for anything white. It took 4 test runs before I got the results I wanted. It’s printed using white and black on gold film with a gloss poly lamination.

3M scotch utility masker 6810 label. This has a vintage 3M logo that dates from the 1960s. I only needed 1 label but always make extra just in case. This was solvent inkjet printed on white adhesive vinyl on a Mimaki CJV150 then laminated with a high gloss poly lamination for durability.
Vintage Baldor 1/2HP grinder labels. The OSHA label must have been used only a short time. I’ve owned a dozen Baldor grinders over the years but only one has this label.
Craftsman 397.19451 3/4HP grinder label with Sears Best label reproductions
Craftsman 397.19681 3/4 HP reproduction grinder label to replace damaged one.

Darex drill sharpener reproduction labels. White printed on clear, black printed on white, and orange and black printed on silver. All with scuff resistant lamination for durability and ease of installation.
Craftsman 397.19440 1/2HP grinder label reproduction printer with red and black on silver gray adhesive vinyl with scuff resistant lamination.
Vintage Craftsman Powr Panl label for on/off switch of a table saw. This is printed in cobalt blue over yellow with a scuff resistant lamination.
A couple of vintage 1970s Baldor grinder labels. These are printed on adhesive vinyl with lamination. Data is printed in black. Originals were on metal with stamped data.
Craftsman motor label model 397.19821 reproduction. The original was embossed but I had no way to reproduce that so this one is flat.

Union Pacific grade crossing decal. This is 23.5” x 5.5” and is printed on a brushed chrome adhesive vinyl with a clear gloss poly lamination. The original was in poor condition snd redrawn as a vector.
Craftsman 115.6962 motor label. This is my first direct metal printed label. It’s digitally printed with UV ink then stamped with 3/32” characters.

Stanley Vidmar cabinet labels. These are on brushed chrome polyester material with a gloss poly lamination. There are two styles - one is a sticker that attaches to the cabinet and the other is on an aluminum plate to fit in the recess at the top of the cabinet. Both have adhesive on the back for easy application. The bumblebee logo took a while to perfect. It has a slight bleed (0.010”) to hide a
Iso Grifo “Lubricants and products to use” reproduction label in English and Italian. These have a 1.5mil clear glossy polyester overlamination applied then are die cut.
Dayton 1Z707 Bench Grinder Label Reproduction
Sears craftsman 397.194011/4 HP grinder label. It makes it a lot easier to get a good reproduction when I have a quality flatbed scan.
Stihl Wood Boss label. The “original” one purchased off of eBay was terrible quality so I reprinted it as a vector file. Having good quality input is what makes for great output.

Nameplates digitally printed onto aluminum sheet using UV curable ink. The detail is amazing and I’m working on fine-tuning the adhesion promoter to withstand heavy scratching. The next batch will have white printed as an under base to add more opacity.
Lisle 91000 drill grinder replacement label for @jackhoying. The old label was so worn that you could only see the serial number.

Craftsman 115.6962 drill press motor reproduction tag. This one was applied to a sheet of 0.020” thick aluminum and the model and serial number were stamped into the metal. You can’t stamp into the label so I left a cut out to keep the stamped areas uncovered.
Milwaukee 806 vise label made from a poor quality photo. I prefer to have a flatbed scan to make a reproduction label, but it’s possible to redo it with just a photo.

Rockwell 15-080 drill press label. This one is applied to a piece of aluminum and new data is stamped using 3/32” character set. Because it is a label applied to aluminum, I had to make a cutout where it gets stamped. So it’s not perfect but I’m happy with the results.
Made a vintage GE motor label for @xbrauerx
Craftsman 397.19580 1/3 HP Grinder Aluminum Label.

Craftsman 397.19590 1/2 HP Bench Grinder Label Replacement. This was printed on clear, laminated with a scuff resistant lamination then applied to a piece of gold brushed aluminum. Corners then rounded and 1/8” holes punched for mounting rivets.
Replacement labels for Craftsman 103.23130 drill press and Craftsman general purpose motor.

Rockwell 438-02-314-0249 grinder label. The light blue required a special spot color “peacock blue” to print. Printed on silver gray adhesive backed vinyl then laminated with an abrasion resistant film for durability.
Vintage Powermatic bandsaw warning label reproduction made from only measurements (6-1/2” x 4-1/2”) and a distorted photo.
Craftsman 397.19391 1/3 HP Grinder Label Reproduction. Old label was completely faded and is getting replaced with a grinder rebuild and restoration.
Craftsman 397.19440 1/2 HP Grinder Label Reproduction
Craftsman 397.19521 grinder label. Original was on metal with stamped data but this is on metallic vinyl with printed data.
Vintage Bosch 6 volt coil label for VW. Printed on adhesive paper and contour cut as oval to better match original label.

Baldor grinder / buffer stand label. This shows the importance of underprinting white below the yellow to add opacity. Otherwise yellow gets washed out. Hard to see until you apply. I didn’t realize the mistake until after I made it and had to redo it.
Gravograph IS8000 engraver label. I pulled out the caliper and pulled measurements off original to get it as close as possible. Font isn’t a perfect match but very close.
Craftsman 397.19340 1/2 HP grinder label
Label for side cover of 1970s Delta Rockwell 6”x48” belt sander 31-520
Craftsman Kromedge Tap and Die Label on Brushed Chrome material
Reproduced a vintage 1/2 HP Craftsman block grinder label that faded away. 397.19370
Craftsman 397.19580 1/3 HP grinder label. This one is 3 colors (black, red, gray) on silver substrate. Originally these were printed on aluminum but I reproduced this one as an adhesive label.
Baldor lighted eye shield warning label (USE 60 WATT LAMP OR LESS 1-405)
Vintage Craftsman block grinder 397.29350 3/4 HP replacement label

Sears Best label reproduction on metallic vinyl printed with opaque white. These were used on vintage craftsman 1 HP block grinders along with other power tools. Some models used a small label below the power switch and others used a larger label above the product label.

USA label sticker on clear vinyl. Printed using white first then red and blue over. Laminated with scuff resistant film for durability. Last image shows the source file. This was all hand drawn using Bézier curve tool and output as spot colors on Gerber Edge 2 printer.
